name: Architectural Privacy Gradient — How Buildings Enable or Prevent the Regulation of Social Accessibility
short_description: Privacy is dynamic regulation of social accessibility; architecture provides five regulatory mechanisms (visual, acoustic, withdrawal, territorial, convention); failure produces crowding stress even at moderate density
structural_pattern: Privacy is a dynamic regulatory process: the continuous adjustment of actual social accessibility toward a desired level (Altman, 1975). The desired level fluctuates with mood, task, personality, time of day, and recent social history. Architecture provides the REGULATORY MECHANISMS. FIVE MECHANISMS: (1) VISUAL PRIVACY — walls, partitions, curtains, screens; (2) ACOUSTIC PRIVACY — walls (STC rating), distance, background masking; (3) SPATIAL WITHDRAWAL — quiet rooms, phone booths, break rooms, outdoor access; (4) TERRITORIAL DEFINITION — assigned desks, personal storage, boundary markers; (5) SOCIAL CONVENTION MARKERS — closed door signals 'do not disturb'. When mechanisms are adequate, occupants maintain social homeostasis (privacy PE ≈ 0). When inadequate, actual accessibility exceeds desired → privacy PE → crowding stress. THE OPEN-PLAN FAILURE: Eliminates ALL FIVE mechanisms simultaneously → maximum privacy PE → maximum crowding stress → the dissatisfaction Kim and de Dear (2013) document. CRITICAL INSIGHT: Crowding is NOT density — it is the PE discrepancy between desired and actual accessibility.
higher_order_principle: Privacy is not a state but a regulation process. Architecture provides the regulatory mechanisms. When mechanisms are adequate, the occupant maintains social homeostasis. When inadequate, regulation fails and chronic discrepancy produces sustained social PE, activating threat/HPA pathway (T5) and contributing to allostatic load (T29). The designer's task is not eliminating social exposure but providing the GRADIENT of exposure settings and MECHANISMS of regulation.

five_privacy_mechanisms.visual_privacy: Walls, partitions, curtains, frosted glass, vegetation, level changes, distance
five_privacy_mechanisms.acoustic_privacy: Walls (STC rating), distance, background masking, absorption, spatial separation
five_privacy_mechanisms.spatial_withdrawal: Quiet rooms, phone booths, break rooms, outdoor terraces, library spaces
five_privacy_mechanisms.territorial_definition: Assigned desks, personal storage, boundary markers, spatial customization
five_privacy_mechanisms.convention_markers: Closed door = do not disturb, pulled curtain = private, occupied phone booth = in conversation

causal_links.evidence_base: Evans & Cohen (1987), Evans & McCoy (1998) demonstrate architectural control mechanisms mediate density-stress relationship. Well-replicated across residential, workplace, institutional settings.

Altman's (1975) regulatory framework directly maps to PE: desired level = prediction; actual = outcome; discrepancy = PE. Supported by density-stress (Evans) and privacy-satisfaction (Kim & de Dear) evidence.
Evans (2003) documents cortisol elevation from chronic density/privacy failure. Attentional fatigue pathway supported by Frith's co-presence cost.
Frith & Frith (2007) establish social processing is automatic and co-presence-dependent.

scope_conditions: Applies to all multi-occupant buildings — workplaces, residences, institutions, healthcare, education
Desired accessibility level varies by individual (introversion/extraversion), culture, task, time of day
Children, elderly, and disabled may have different privacy regulation needs
Digital privacy (email monitoring, screen visibility) adds layer not addressed by physical-spatial focus
moderators: Introversion/extraversion: introverts have lower optimal social exposure levels
Task type: complex cognitive work requires more privacy than routine manual work
Organizational culture: some value open collaboration; others value focused individual work
Tenure and familiarity: new employees need more privacy regulation than established teams
Time of day: privacy needs typically increase through workday as social fatigue accumulates

interactions.nature: SC4 describes encounter benefits of spatial integration. SOC2 describes privacy costs. Good design balances both.
Privacy failure consumes directed attention (T25). Co-presence and acoustic transparency deplete the same attentional resource ART seeks to restore.
Acoustic privacy failure forces continuous auditory scene analysis (T31).
Sustained privacy PE activates threat/HPA pathway (T5).
Chronic privacy failure → sustained social PE → allostatic load (T29).
